thread:
Lara H: quick check — running into a weird client behavior when both REDWOOD_PRIVATE_ENDPOINT and HTTP_PROXY are set in our k8s sidecar. Streaming requests start, then after ~20s reconnects fail with 502. Anyone seen this combo?
Sam G: I saw something similar last month when SNI was mismatched. Are you rewriting Host headers in the proxy?
Lara H: we aren't rewriting. proxy is a small aws nlb -> envoy passthrough, but REDWOOD_PRIVATE_ENDPOINT is a hostname like private-api.redwood.internal:443.
Mike (devex): env var precedence: our SDK uses explicit client config > REDWOOD_BASE_URL > REDWOOD_PRIVATE_ENDPOINT fallback. But streaming path may open a separate connection path that uses raw socket SNI from the host portion.
Lara H: ah interesting — so if proxy strips SNI or rewrites it, TLS handshake might go to wrong cert. envoy was in tcp mode so shouldn't touch SNI though.
Ankit: can you paste the minimal client init? e.g.:
```
new RedwoodClient({ baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_PRIVATE_ENDPOINT, apiKey: KEY, streaming: true, retry: { maxRetries: 3 } })
```
Julie P: FYI infra-bot showed a few NAT timeouts around the same window (infra-bot: noted 2 ephemeral node restarts in that AZ). Could be unrelated.
Lara H: repro steps: plain http streaming works against public API, only private endpoint + proxy combo fails. Curl with --http2 works, but our Node SDK stream gets mid-request 502 on reconnect.
Mike (devex): quick checklist: 1) confirm envoy passthrough preserves SNI (tcp forward preserves but check TLS termination config), 2) ensure Host header is the private hostname when using an HTTP proxy (some libs set Host to proxy host), 3) increase keepalive so proxy doesn't recycle idle connection, 4) enable client retry jitter/backoff for streaming reconnects.
Sam G: also check that your proxy isn't doing transparent HTTP/1.1 upgrade dance — streaming expects http/2. If proxy downgrades to http/1.1 it could break streaming frames.
Lara H: good call. Where's the place in our SDK to force http2 for streaming connect?
Mike (devex): Node SDK: passing `transport: { preferHttp2: true }` in client opts forces http2 and will fall back if the proxy refuses. For Java and Go we have similar flags. I'll drop a short snippet in the repo.
Ankit: as a short-term workaround, can we set `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` to the proxy URL (including :443) and set `disableProxy: true` in the pod for that client? Might avoid double-proxying.
Julie P: if you disable the node-level HTTP_PROXY env the SDK will still talk to baseUrl directly. That worked for a similar case where the cluster egress proxy added headers that confused our routing.
Lara H: thanks — trying `preferHttp2` + increase keepalive and disabling cluster HTTP_PROXY for the pod now. Will report back.
Mike (devex): if it still fails, capture a TLS handshake with `openssl s_client -connect private-api.redwood.internal:443 -servername private-api.redwood.internal -alpn h2` and paste output. That'll show SNI/ALPN.
Lara H: one more question — for auth: when using private endpoints should we still send the Authorization header or rely on mTLS? We have mTLS enabled on the private load balancer.
Sam G: mTLS is mandatory for some enterprise customers but our SDK currently expects apiKey unless you pass `useMtls: true` which will use client cert and skip sending apiKey header. Behavior is documented but easy to miss.
Mike (devex): note: when `useMtls: true` is on we still include a short `x-client-id` header for telemetry; nothing sensitive.
Lara H: sweet. thanks everyone. I'll update with logs and the openssl output if it persists. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: scheduled-maintenance: No planned maintenance in the next 48h affecting that AZ. (auto-note)
Mike (devex): pinging @Julie P and @Ankit for infra follow-ups if Lara's capture shows SNI loss — we may need a docs note about proxy+private-endpoint pitfalls.
Julie P: noted, will draft a short devex note after Lara's repro.
Lara H: follow-up: after forcing http2 and disabling POD HTTP_PROXY, streaming stable. Re-enabling proxy + http2 caused the 502s again. I'll open an issue with tcpdump/openssl traces.
Mike (devex): perfect — thanks! I'll link the issue to the SDK changelog so we can add a debug tip in the README.
